tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Components of Fitness

questions.question: Define cardiovascular endurance and give a sporting example where it is the most important component.
questions.correctAnswer: Cardiovascular endurance is the ability of the heart, lungs and blood vessels to deliver oxygen to working muscles over a prolonged period. Example: marathon running, where the athlete must sustain aerobic exercise for over 26 miles.

questions.question: Explain the difference between strength and power.
questions.correctAnswer: Strength is the maximum force a muscle can exert in a single maximal contraction. Power is the ability to exert a maximal force in the shortest possible time (strength × speed). Strength involves maximum force regardless of speed; power requires force to be applied QUICKLY.

questions.question: Define agility and give two sporting examples.
questions.correctAnswer: Agility is the ability to change direction quickly and precisely while maintaining balance and control. Examples: a footballer dribbling past a defender with quick changes of direction; a tennis player changing direction to reach a wide shot.

Explain the difference between static and dynamic balance, giving a sporting example of each.
questions.correctAnswer: Static balance is maintaining the body's centre of mass above the base of support while stationary (e.g. a gymnast holding a handstand on the beam). Dynamic balance is maintaining the body's centre of mass above the base of support while moving (e.g. a rugby player staying on their feet while being tackled).

questions.question: Define reaction time and explain why it is important for a sprinter at the start of a race.
questions.correctAnswer: Reaction time is the time taken to initiate a response to a stimulus. For a sprinter, it is the time between hearing the starting gun and beginning to push off the blocks. A faster reaction time means the sprinter gets out of the blocks sooner, giving them an advantage in a race decided by hundredths of a second.
